title.en: Retail trade: itinerant and fixed-shop retailers

hook.en: From the vegetable vendor's cart to a giant mall, retailers are where goods finally meet consumers.

objectives.en: Describe itinerant retailers and small fixed-shop retailers
Describe large-scale retailers: departmental stores, chain stores and others

narration.en: From the vegetable vendor's cart to a giant mall, retailers are where goods finally meet consumers.

body.en: A retailer buys from wholesalers or producers and sells in small quantities to the final consumer. To consumers, retailers offer regular availability of goods, a choice of products, information about new products, convenient location and hours, after-sales service and sometimes credit. To producers and wholesalers, they help in distribution, carry out personal selling and promotion, and pass on market information about consumers' wants.

points.en: Sells to final consumers in small quantities
Helps producers with distribution and feedback

title.en: On the board: types of retailers

say.en: Itinerant retailers: no fixed place of business.

text.en: types of retailers
Peddlers and hawkers, market traders (weekly haats),
street traders (pavements), cheap jacks (temporary shops)
General stores, single-line stores, speciality stores,
street stalls, second-hand goods shops
Departmental stores: many departments under one roof
Chain stores (multiple shops): many branches, one owner
Supermarkets, consumer cooperative stores, mail-order
houses

narration.en: Let us build up types of retailers on the board, one step at a time.

text.en: A vendor who carries vegetables from street to street
A neighbourhood general store
A store with clothing, grocery and electronics departments under one roof
A shoe company's 200 branches across India
A trader at the weekly village haat
A shop that sells only spectacles

explanation.en: Itinerant retailers move; small shops have one fixed outlet; large retailers run big stores or many branches.

body.en: A departmental store is a large establishment with many departments, each selling a different line, under one roof and one management, usually in a central location: it offers a wide variety and services, but has high costs and higher prices. Chain stores (multiple shops) are a network of identical branches owned by one firm, selling standardised goods at uniform prices; they buy centrally in bulk, so costs are lower, but they offer a limited range and little credit. Shopping malls and online stores now compete with both.

points.en: Departmental: many lines, one roof, central location
Chain: many branches, standard goods, uniform prices

Branches in many localities
Uniform prices in all outlets

explanation.en: A departmental store brings many goods to one place; a chain store takes one kind of goods to many places.

problem.en: Why do itinerant traders survive in Indian towns and villages?

steps.en: They bring goods to the customer's doorstep: great convenience.
They need very little capital and have low costs, so prices are low.
They sell daily necessities such as vegetables, fruit and household items.
They serve areas and people that big shops do not reach.

answer.en: Convenience, low cost and reach keep itinerant traders relevant.
